title: RyR2 Dysfunction in Ventricular Arrhythmogenesis and Emerging Evidence for Dantrolene
content: Ryanodine receptor 2 (RyR2) is a key regulator of intracellular Ca2+ handling and cardiac excitation-contraction coupling, and its dysfunction has emerged as an important driver of ventricular arrhythmogenesis. In pathological states, hyperactive or “leaky” RyR2 channels promote abnormal sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) Ca2+ release, electrical instability, and ventricular tachyarrhythmias. Despite increasing recognition of intracellular Ca2+ dysregulation as a central arrhythmogenic mechanism, most current anti-arrhythmic therapies primarily target sarcolemmal ion channels rather than intracellular Ca2+ handling. This review examines the molecular mechanisms underlying RyR2 dysfunction, with particular focus on the context-dependent effects of dantrolene in pathologies characterized by diastolic Ca2+ leak and arrhythmogenic susceptibility. We evaluate preclinical and emerging clinical evidence supporting dantrolene-mediated RyR2 stabilization as a potential therapeutic strategy for RyR2-mediated arrhythmias and discuss the translational limitations and future directions of mechanism-based therapies targeting intracellular Ca2+ dynamics.
